answer: Each agent must stake a bond before it can act, and each new identity pays a registration fee set at a fixed fraction of that bond. A sybil farm can mint endless keys for free, so identity proves nothing; what it cannot cheaply fake is many funded, slashable stakes. When an address misbehaves, peers vote and its bond is slashed, burning value already paid. Splitting into many identities multiplies fees, so cheating costs more. This is no marble trick: the market prices a vertex of trust as capital at risk, letting honest agents wander freely.
